headline: Approved $937,409 firefighter union contract funding and four utility conduit grants; referred rodenticide ban and $332,497 Tufts Street soil fund to committees.
summary: The council approved four utility conduit requests on Grand Union Boulevard, Taylor Street, Charlestown Street, and Prescott Street. It approved $937,409 for a firefighter union contract and referred a rodenticide ordinance and a $332,497 Tufts Street soil fund to committees.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the June 25, 2026 regular meeting.
Approved the remembrances (moments of silence) requested by councilors.
Approved citation commending Dan Amelin for eight years of service in the Engineering Division.
Approved citation commending Ramón Bueno for his commitment to climate action.
Approved citation commending Eliza Johnston for her commitment to climate action.
Approved Lightpath Grant of Location to install 41 feet of conduit in Grand Union Boulevard.
Approved Eversource Grant of Location to install 208 feet of conduit in Taylor Street and Sydney Street.
Approved Eversource Grant of Location to install 201 feet of conduit in Charlestown Street and Allen Street.
Approved Eversource Grant of Location to install 51 feet of conduit in Prescott Street.
Approved an order to schedule a public hearing on establishing civilian oversight of the Police Department.
Referred the ordinance to ban certain rodenticides (Chapter 6 of the Code of Ordinances) to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation.
Approved resolution to end the Supplemental Nutrition Assistant Program access crisis.
Approved resolution in support of a fair and dignified resolution for an international graduate student at Tufts University.
Approved resolution in support of security officers in Greater Boston and airport service workers at Logan International Airport.
Approved resolution in support of Service Employees International Union 32BJ facilities workers at Tufts University.
Approved resolution asking the Director of Health and Human Services to discuss street harassment on Prescott Street, School Street, and near the Warming Center, and sent it for discussion.
Approved order asking the Director of Inspectional Services for a report on short-term rentals, and sent it for discussion.
Approved resolution on short-term rental reporting instructions and a 311 category for illegal rentals, and sent it for discussion.
Approved resolution asking the Director of Planning to work with the council to increase accessible housing.
Approved resolution asking the Administration to organize another city-wide neighborhood trash pickup this fall.
Approved resolution in support of retaining Route 80 service through Somerville.
Approved resolution asking the Director of Mobility to consider street painting near Belmont Street and Spring Hill Terrace.
Approved resolution to increase pay for crossing guards.
Resolution supporting a state-authorized Cultural District in East Somerville was withdrawn.
Referred the Mayor's request for a Home Rule Petition to regulate anticoagulant rodenticides to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation.
Referred the Mayor's request to amend Section 1-11(b) of the Code of Ordinances on enforcement personnel to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to create the Tufts Street Soil Project Stabilization Fund and accept $332,497 from Unifirst Corporation to the Finance Committee for recommendation.

Approved the appropriation of $937,409 from the Salary Contingency Account for the Firefighters Association of Somerville, Local 76 Union contract, by a 10-0 vote with Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait absent.
Referred the request to appropriate $332,497 from the Tufts Street Soil Project Stabilization Fund for 50 Tufts Street remediation to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to use $8,800 from Police Salaries for Deputy Chief cost of living increases to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to transfer $315,000 from the Sewer Enterprise Debt Service Account to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to transfer $60,000 for temporary clerical staffing to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Approved a $1,000 inter-fund transfer from the Sewer Enterprise Debt Service Account to the Somerville Avenue Infrastructure Improvement Sewer Capital Fund Union Square Sewer Bond Account.
Approved a $1,000 inter-fund transfer from the Sewer Enterprise Debt Service Account to the Spring Hill Sewer Separation Project Design Capital Fund.
Approved a $1,000 inter-fund transfer from the Sewer Enterprise Debt Service Account to the Poplar Street Pump Station Design Capital Fund.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $366,729.25 Metropolitan Area Planning Council grant for Bluebikes equipment to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $284,700 Massachusetts Gaming Commission grant for the Eastern Washington Street Transit Priority Project to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $187,200.00 Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness Grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend an $85,933.60 Bluebikes equipment grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $65,000 Mass Department of Mental Health grant for the Metro Boston Crisis Intervention Training center to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $20,239 Bureau of Justice Assistance grant for World Cup 2026 overtime to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $12,000 Mass Department of Mental Health grant for the jail/arrest diversion program to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Approved acceptance of a gift of 200 soccer balls worth about $5,000 from the United States Conference of Mayors.
Referred the request to pay a prior year invoice of $3,572 for ArcGIS Urban to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Approved confirmation of Chanthan Neang as Police Officer.
Approved confirmation of Isaiah Saint-Vil as Police Officer.
Approved confirmation of Joshua Benson as Police Officer.
Approved confirmation of Christian Marsden as Police Officer.
Approved confirmation of Odamarys Pamela Acosta as Police Officer.
Approved confirmation of Michael Avery to the Elections Commission.
Motion by Councilor Mbah to reconsider the approval of Michael Avery's Elections Commission appointment failed.
Approved confirmation of Mary Otiato to the Commission for Persons with Disabilities.
Approved exemption for Mark Antonelli under Massachusetts General Law Chapter 268A, § 20(b).
Referred the Technology-Specific Surveillance Use Policy for Body Worn Cameras to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation.
Referred the Surveillance Technology Impact Report for Body Worn Cameras to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation.
Approved proclamation of July 2026 as South Asian Heritage Month in Somerville.
Approved proclamation of August 26, 2026 as Women's Equality Day in Somerville.
Placed on file and sent for discussion the Planning Board recommendations for item 26-0835.

Placed on file the School Committee appointment of Jack Perenick to the Ranked Choice Voting Committee.

Placed on file the School Committee appointment of Devon Moos to the Public Financing of Campaigns Committee.
Placed on file the City Clerk's report of Block Party Licenses issued.

# City of Somerville, Massachusetts · City Council · Meeting Minutes

Thursday, August 27, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:00 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered recess at 7:03 PM and returned at 7:19 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 7:42 PM and returned at 7:44 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 8:04 PM and returned at 8:07 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 9:48 PM and returned at 10:24 PM.

1.1. Roll Call

Call of the Roll.

## (ID # 26-1324 ) RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

- Present: Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen
- City Councilor At Large Jon Link
- Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott
- Ward Four City Councilor Jesse Clingan
- City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo
- City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler
- Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt
- Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin
- City Councilor At Large Wilfred N. Mbah
- Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis

## Absent:

Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1325 )

- Councilor McLaughlin requested a moment of silence in memory of Jo-Ann
- Fontano.

- Councilor Hardt requested a moment of silence in memory of Edwin
- Jeovanny Lopez Cornejo, Prisciliano Trejo Ricano, Juan Jairo Coronilla
- Duran, Jesus Manuel Arenas-Silva, Joan Sebastian Guerrero and Lorenzo

Salgado Araujo, who died as result of being detained by a federal immigration agency.

Councilor Wheeler and Councilor Ewen- Campen requested a moment of silence in memory of Lawrence “Larry” Aronson.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Michael
- Chiapperini.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of William
- Fitzpatrick.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Jesse
- Gregory.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of lives lost
- due to the extreme flooding in Nepal.

## RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Regular Meeting of June 25, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1326 ) RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

2.1. Citation

By Councilor Ewen-Campen

(ID # 26-1251 ) Commending Dan Amelin for eight years of service in the Engineering

Division.

- Councilor Ewen-Campen presented Mr. Amelin with a citation recognizing

his work on several complex projects in the city. Mr. Amelin thanked his colleagues for their contributions to the successful completion of those

- projects.

## RESULT: APPROVED

2.2. Citation

By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1312 ) Commending Ramón Bueno for his commitment to climate action.

- Councilor Mbah presented Mr. Bueno with a citation recognizing his nine

years of service to the City. Mr. Bueno thanked the Council for the recognition and reflected on his work under three city administrations.

## RESULT: APPROVED

2.3. Citation

By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1313 ) Commending Eliza Johnston for her commitment to climate action.

- Councilor Mbah presented Ms. Johnston with a citation recognizing her 17

years of service to the City. Ms. Johnston thanked the Council for the recognition and expressed her appreciation to city staff for their expertise and cooperation.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

3.1. Grant of Location Lightpath applying for a Grant of Location to install 41 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1278 ) Grand Union Boulevard, from existing telephone conduit near the intersection of Revolution Drive and Grand Union Boulevard to a point of pickup at existing Manhole 29310 next to 188 Assembly Park Drive.

Jeffery Harrington, representing Lightpath, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.2. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 208 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1275 ) Taylor Street and Sydney Street and one new Manhole 32883, from Utility

- Pole 387/4 passing through the new Manhole 32883 to a point of pickup at 9
- Taylor Street.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.3. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 201 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1276 ) Charlestown Street and Allen Street, from proposed Manhole 32885 to a

point of pickup at 37 Allen Street.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

Councilor Scott asked why the right-of-way needed to be excavated. Ms.

Duffy explained that a new manhole was required to service the project.

- Councilor Scott requested that Eversource explore alternatives that would
- avoid opening the street, if feasible.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.4. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 51 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1277 ) Prescott Street, from Utility Pole 287/8 to a point of pickup at 53 Prescott

Street.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Order

By Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1321 ) In his capacity as President, that this Council schedule a Public Hearing

regarding the establishment of an entity to provide civilian oversight of the Police Department.

President Davis reported that he had discussed civilian oversight of the Police Department with the Administration and stated that this item

- represents the first step in the process.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.2. Ordinance

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Link, Councilor Clingan and Councilor

(ID # 26-1310 ) Mbah

That Chapter 6 of the Code of Ordinances be amended as detailed within.

- Councilor Hardt explained that the ordinance would ban the use of certain

rodenticides and noted that these products are not effective in controlling rat populations. She invited Morgan Penny of Save Somerville Wildlife to speak on the matter. Ms. Penny discussed the harmful and often fatal effects of rodenticides on birds of prey and other wildlife and requested that the City pursue a Home Rule Petition to ban their use. Councilor Link spoke

about the need to control the rat population and emphasized the importance of protecting natural predators as part of that effort.

- Councilors Clingan, Councilor Scott, and Councilor Wheeler spoke about

the harmful effects of rodenticides, the need to protect wildlife, and the importance of eliminating rats’ access to food.

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Legislative Matters Committee

4.3. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor

(ID # 26-1301 ) Link, Councilor Strezo, Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Clingan, Councilor

- Davis and Councilor McLaughlin
- To end the Supplemental Nutrition Assistant Program access crisis.

- Councilor Hardt commented on the redistribution of wealth and expressed

concern that collective wealth is being concentrated among the wealthiest individuals in the country. She reported that 91.5% of callers to the Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA) were unable to reach the assistance they needed and noted that, due to limited capacity to process

- applications, Somerville’s Supplemental Nutrition Assistant Program

(SNAP) caseload had decreased by 15%. Councilor Mbah spoke about the impact on households and noted that the resolution calls on the state to hire additional caseworkers to address the crisis.

- Councilor Hardt sponsored Ray Santana, President of the Mystic Tenant

Association, to speak on the matter. Ms. Santana spoke about the urgent need for DTA benefits and the challenges caused by under-staffing, including families going without food for weeks. She also read a letter from another association member describing the frustrations experienced while

- attempting to access benefits.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.4. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor

(ID # 26-1302 ) Scott, Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Wheeler and Councilor Clingan

In support of a fair and dignified resolution for an international graduate student at Tufts University.

Councilor Mbah explained that the resolution is intended to address the ongoing consequences faced by the student involved. He stated that the City has a responsibility to uphold academic integrity, due process, and freedom from retaliation, and that the resolution therefore calls on Tufts University to mitigate the academic and financial harm the student has experienced as a

result of the matter. Councilor Hardt commented on the precarious position of international students. Councilor Wheeler noted that the Council does not have all of the particulars of the incident.

Councilor Mbah sponsored Chris Mollinari to address the Council. Mr.

Mollinari, a steward for the Tufts University Graduate Workers Union, described the circumstances surrounding the incident and reported that the student had decided to continue her education at another institution rather than remain at Tufts.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Strezo, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor

(ID # 26-1303 ) Link, Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Davis, Councilor

- Clingan and Councilor McLaughlin

In support of security officers in Greater Boston and airport service workers at Logan International Airport.

- Councilor Mbah explained that this resolution calls upon property owners

and security clients to support the security officers guarding their buildings and to publicly urge the security contractors they hire to bargain fairly and in good faith and to provide quality, affordable healthcare to these officers, and also calls on Massport to institute a policy requiring airlines and their

service contractors at Logan International Airport to provide quality, affordable healthcare to airport service workers.

- Councilor Mbah sponsored Stanley Warshen, a security guard, to speak on

the item. He spoke about the need for health care benefits, saying that bargaining negotiations are dragging on and he stated that workers are just asking for fair contracts with affordable health care.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.6. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Strezo, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor

(ID # 26-1304 ) Link, Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Clingan, Councilor

- McLaughlin and Councilor Davis

In support of Service Employees International Union 32BJ facilities workers at Tufts University.

Through this resolution, the City Council stands in solidarity with the Service Employees International Union 32BJ facilities workers at Tufts

University and urges Tufts University to reach a fair and timely agreement that provides family-sustaining wages, affordable healthcare, strong benefits, and appropriate workplace protections. Councilor Mbah sponsored James

Goode, grounds keeper at Tufts, to address the Council. Mr. Goode stated that the contract expired on July 1, and that the negotiations that began in April have not been productive. He asked for the Council’s support as his

union attempts to secure adequate annual wage increases and affordable healthcare.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.12. Resolution

By Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Clingan, Councilor McLaughlin, (ID # 26-1314 ) Councilor Hardt, Councilor Wheeler and Councilor Link

In support of retaining Route 80 service through Somerville.

- Councilor Ewen-Campen addressed the Massachusetts Bay Transportation
- Authority's (MBTA) proposed elimination of Route 80 service, which the

MBTA considers redundant due to the Green Line Extension (GLX). He noted that there are strong arguments to the contrary and that the MBTA was accepting public comments on this and several other proposed service

changes through September 8. He urged residents to submit comments and suggested searching online for “Better Bus Network public feedback” to find links to a survey, email, and mailing address.

Councilor Ewen-Campen sponsored Alessandra Seiter, Chair of Somerville’s Pedestrian and Transit Advisory Committee (PTAC), to address the Council. Ms. Seiter highlighted the importance of Route 80 to Somerville, including its connection between Magoun Square and East

- Somerville and its service to the future school building on Sycamore Street.

She noted that Route 80 provides reliable, affordable, and accessible public transportation to key locations, including Gilman Square, Pearl Street Park, and Western Pearl Street, as well as to neighborhoods with some of the City’s most economically and socially vulnerable residents.

Ms. Seiter explained that under the MBTA’s ongoing bus network redesign, Route 80 is slated to be removed from Medford Street and Pearl Street, leaving the Gilman Square and East Somerville communities without an

accessible transit option for residents with disabilities or a service that meets the needs of neighborhood school populations. She encouraged members of the public to submit comments to betterbusproject@mbta.com.
